public_rationale: Both contract values match his figures: about $1.25 billion for Sharon AI/ESDS and $44.6 million for KIDZ AI/Canopy Wave. Whether capex is 'barely paid off' depends on the real capital cost, and he used his own estimate: about $550,000 per 8-GPU pod, doubled for the facility. Search snippets of SharonAI's SEC filings put expected capex for the ESDS deal at about $720 million. That would make contract value about 1.75 times capex, which is not 'barely'. But those filings could not be read, so the figure cannot be cited. No capex was found for the KIDZ cluster. With no citable capex for either project, the claim stays unresolved.
limitations: The key SharonAI capex figure is known only from search snippets and is not cited.
The Sharon AI cluster sits in an existing leased data center, which may make facility costs opex rather than capex. That would undercut his doubling assumption, but no cited source quantifies it.
Even with full data, 'barely' has no fixed margin.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: In the Sharon AI and Catalyst Compute contracts, capex is barely paid off over five years even ignoring opex and debt.

statement.excerpt: In both of these cases, capital expenditures are barely paid off in five years, and only if you don’t include a single dollar of operating expenses or associated debt.

from_speaker: "In both of these cases": the Sharon AI/ESDS contract (8,208 B300s at $3.30 an hour for five years, about $1.264 billion) and the Catalyst Compute/Canopy Wave contract (256 B300s, about $44.6 million)
"capital expenditures are barely paid off in five years"
"only if you don't include a single dollar of operating expenses or associated debt"
his capex inputs: about $550,000 per 8-GPU B300 pod, with 'the capex' for the facility 'a comparable amount', giving about $1.1 billion and about $35 million
our_interpretation: This is an appraisal of the two contracts as signed and disclosed before the post. The test compares each contract's full five-year value, assuming full payment, with the project's actual or company-disclosed capital cost. Disclosures from the contract signings onward count, including any mid-2026 project budget.

'Barely paid off' is read as five-year contract revenue only modestly above capex: roughly up to a third more, as with his own figures of $1.264 billion vs $1.1 billion and $44.6 million vs $35 million. Revenue far above capex (for example, 1.5 times or more) would contradict it.

The second part ('only if you don't include ... opex or debt') is read as saying that once operating costs and financing costs are added, five-year receipts would not cover total cost. It is tested only if capex, opex, and debt cost data are available.
Capex counts only what the contract holder actually spends. If a provider rents space in an existing data center, facility costs are operating expenses, not capex.
criteria.support_condition: Disclosed capital cost for each project sits close to its five-year contract value: the contract exceeds capex only modestly, and adding reasonable opex and financing costs would leave no surplus.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Disclosed capital cost for either or both projects sits well below the five-year contract value (for example, contract value 1.5 times capex or more), so capex is clearly more than 'barely' recovered before opex and debt.
